headline: SCHOOL ADMINISTRATOR’S GUIDE TO OKLAHOMA’S IMMUNIZATION LAW
blurb: Oklahoma's legislature added immunization requirements for school attendance to the state school code in 1970.

headline: Food-borne Hepatitis A -- Oklahoma, Texas
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: A hepatitis A outbreak in Marietta, Oklahoma, made 203 people ill between August 15 and October 10, 1983, and most of the patients who were interviewed had eaten at one drive-in restaurant.

headline: Epidemiologic Notes and Reports Pertussis Outbreak -- Oklahoma
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Oklahoma reported 330 whooping cough cases from January 1 through December 10, 1983, with cases peaking in June and July.

headline: Outbreaks of hepatitis A among illicit drug users, Oklahoma, 1984-87
blurb: Oklahoma State Department of Health staff described six unrelated hepatitis A outbreaks among people who used marijuana and injected methamphetamine.

headline: SCHOOL ADMINISTRATOR’S GUIDE TO OKLAHOMA’S IMMUNIZATION LAW
blurb: Starting in fall 1990, Oklahoma added a second dose of MMR vaccine to its school requirements, beginning with children entering kindergarten.

headline: 292 cases reported in Garfield County mumps outbreak
blurb: The Oklahoma State Department of Health counted 292 mumps cases in Garfield County, part of a statewide outbreak of 342 cases.

headline: First Cases of Measles in Oklahoma Reported
blurb: Oklahoma's health department reported two probable measles cases in people who said they were exposed in the Texas and New Mexico outbreak.
